- claim-1: \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has integral Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution preserving Littlewood–Richardson multiplication under conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: For the conjugate non-self-conjugate inputs \([222,4^5]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) and \([33,5^4]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{4,5}\), complete \(A_+J\)-relation matrices and quotient Smith data in degrees \(6,\ldots,20\) agree: free-rank sequence \((1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) and no torsion in either case. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]
- claim-3: Conditional on the accepted ideal correspondence \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), conjugation induces a graded integral isomorphism \[ J_v/A_+J_v\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}. \] Consequently it preserves every degreewise torsion subgroup and free rank.
## Strategy
Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\), \(q=n-r\), with positive ideals \(A_+\) and \(A^\vee_+\). Partition conjugation induces the integral graded ring isomorphism
\[
\Phi:A\to A^\vee,\qquad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'},
\]
because \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\); \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]. It preserves partition weight.

Conditional on the accepted ideal correspondence \(\Phi(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), grading gives \(\Phi(A_+)=A^\vee_+\), hence
\[
\Phi(A_+J_v)=A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Therefore \(\Phi\) descends degreewise to
\[
(J_v/A_+J_v)_d\cong(J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee})_d.
\]
Each is an integral-group isomorphism, so it identifies torsion subgroups and preserves free \(\mathbb Z\)-ranks, including zero degrees and the \(a=0\) singleton-family boundary.
